copyright_line_on_page: The NASA Image and Video Library item page shows no copyright notice (center: JSC). NASA's media usage guidelines (https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/) say NASA content 'generally are not subject to copyright in the United States'.
title: International Space Station Cameras Capture New Views Of Hurricane Milton
place: Hurricane Milton over the Gulf of Mexico, seen from the International Space Station
audio: silent track (approx. -85 dB), kept as AAC
notes: One continuous static shot 0-14 s: the whole hurricane spiral with a small, sharp eye below the curved Earth horizon and black space above; an ISS module fills the right ~25% of the frame (x 0.75-1.0) and some station hardware sits at bottom centre (x 0.42-0.65, bottom 6%). The clouds move very slowly, so it is close to a still. Eye at about x=0.45, y=0.63. Square crop centred at x~0.45 keeps the eye and the storm and cuts most of the module (its left edge stays in the square). Every second is equally usable; 0-7 and 7-14 are fine. Source is 1280x720 at 59.94 fps (the ~large rendition; the ~orig file is 404 MB), upscaled to 1920x1080 at 30 fps. No people, no text, no logos (the NASA logo appears only at the very end of the original, not in this cut). Alternative in the same source: 16-30 s is a wider, closer view where the pinhole eye sits at x~0.45, with no station hardware.
fact_en: NASA: cameras on the ISS captured Category 4 Hurricane Milton at 9:37 a.m. EDT on October 8; 'As of 8 a.m. EDT on Oct. 8, Milton was packing winds of 145 miles an hours [sic] and strengthening.'
